result:
Perfect! I've successfully implemented Japanese language support for the blog application. Here's what I've accomplished:

## Implementation Summary

### Translation Files
- **`lang/en/messages.json`**: Created English translations for all required UI labels
- **`lang/ja/messages.json`**: Created Japanese translations matching the English structure

### Backend Changes
- **`app/Http/Controllers/LocaleController.ts`**: New endpoint handler for POST /locale that sets a cookie to remember language preference
- **`app/Http/Validators/LocaleValidator.ts`**: Validator ensuring only valid locales ('en', 'ja') are accepted
- **`src/app.ts`**: Added 'ja' to supported locales and registered I18nProvider
- **`app/Providers/I18nProvider.ts`**: New provider that shares `_i18n` props with all pages, containing locale and translation catalog
- **`routes/web.ts`**: Added POST /locale route with validation

### Frontend Changes
- **`resources/js/components/Layout.tsx`**: 
  - Added language switcher (EN/JA buttons) in header
  - Implemented dot-notation translation lookup for nested objects
  - Updated all navigation labels to use translations

- **`resources/js/pages/posts/Index.tsx`**: Updated search button to use translations

- **`resources/js/pages/posts/Show.tsx`**: Updated edit and delete buttons to use translations

### Features Delivered
✅ Two languages: English (default) and Japanese  
✅ Language switcher on every page for guests and logged-in users  
✅ Language selection persists via HTTP cookie (1-year expiration)  
✅ User redirected back to their current page after language selection  
✅ First-time visitors follow browser's Accept-Language header  
✅ Invalid locale values fail validation like other form errors  
✅ All UI labels read from translation catalogs (no hard-coded text)  
✅ English and Japanese catalogs in perfect sync (all 10 keys match)  
✅ `bun run typecheck` passes  
✅ `bun test` passes  
✅ `bun run guren check --i18n` passes
